title: Outlook for iOS and Android: Purview label inheritance from email attachments
summary: The briefing passes: its policy controls, commands and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft's documentation. It accurately reports the disagreement between the launched roadmap item and Learn's mobile support table, without inventing minimum app versions or rollout instructions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: According to the roadmap, mobile Outlook can automatically apply an email sensitivity label from labeled attachments according to organizational policy.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: According to the roadmap, mobile Outlook can recommend an email sensitivity label from labeled attachments according to organizational policy.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the feature reduces manual labeling effort.
claims.quote: This helps organizations maintain consistent data classification and protection while reducing manual labeling effort.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Attachment inheritance requires an administrator to enable it in the label policy, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the **Default settings for emails** page. For the section **Inherit label from attachments**, select the checkbox **Email inherits highest priority label from attachments**.

claims.claim: The entitlement is included in the documented Purview sensitivity labeling licenses, rather than a separately documented attachment-inheritance product.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview service description states that sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy‑based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service description's table also lists manual sensitivity labeling as included in Microsoft 365 E3 and several other plans.
claims.quote: | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Using sensitivity labels in Office apps requires a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches the Email inherits highest priority label from attachments checkbox.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the **Default settings for emails** page. For the section **Inherit label from attachments**, select the checkbox **Email inherits highest priority label from attachments**.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} configures automatic inheritance.
claims.quote: Set the value to **Automatic** (to automatically apply the label) or **Recommended** (as a recommended prompt to the user. Example: `Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}`.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: **Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.**

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} configures a recommendation instead of automatic application.
claims.quote: **AttachmentAction**: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to **Automatic** (to automatically apply the label) or **Recommended** (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: These settings are per label policy and apply to the users and groups selected for that policy.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: Inheritance dynamically selects an email label from sensitivity labels on attachments that are published to the user.
claims.quote: With this configuration, a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: The highest priority eligible attachment label is selected when supported by Outlook.
claims.quote: The [highest priority label](sensitivity-labels#label-priority-order-matters) is dynamically selected when it's supported by Outlook.

claims.claim: Attachment inheritance does not replace a manually applied email label.
claims.quote: When an email message has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by label inheritance from email attachments.

claims.claim: Attachment inheritance replaces a lower priority automatically applied label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Attachment inheritance replaces a lower priority default label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Attachment inheritance does not override a higher priority email label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The attachment must be a physical file.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Links to SharePoint or OneDrive files do not qualify as attachments for this inheritance setting.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.claim: The recommendation option becomes available after selecting the inheritance checkbox.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: **Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.**

claims.claim: With inheritance enabled and recommendation not selected, the label is automatically applied.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Learn says users can remove the automatically inherited label before sending.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Learn says users can select a different label before sending.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: By default, the automatically selected label's encryption is also applied to the email.
claims.quote: By default, if the automatically selected label applies encryption, the same encryption is applied to the email.

claims.claim: Learn describes DKE cases in which no label or encryption is selected for the email.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Learn describes no email label or protection being selected when the highest priority label applies only user-defined permissions for Word, PowerPoint and Excel.
claims.quote: no label or protection is selected for the email message because Outlook doesn't support this label configuration.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Outlook for iOS and Android require an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Windows, Outlook for iOS and Android, Outlook on the web, and new Outlook for Windows, the mailbox must be hosted in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: Outlook for iOS and Android sensitivity labeling does not support on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Windows, Outlook for iOS and Android, Outlook on the web, and new Outlook for Windows, the mailbox must be hosted in Exchange Online. Sensitivity labels aren't supported for mailboxes that are hosted on-premises.
